agentCan: Implement the App Login Flow (launchpad login, token exchange, per-installation apiEndPoint handling, userinfo)
Prepare all app and publisher values, and the verification packet (test access, paging/rate-limit behavior)

approval.cost: No fee mentioned in the docs read (unverified whether any exists)
approval.trigger: Pre-verification, an 'In development' app 'can only be used by the Teamwork.com account it was created under': the pre-approval cap is effectively one account, your own. To publish, email integrations@teamwork.com to kick off verification; Teamwork checks the app against its checklist and sends it to QA for testing. QA checks: clear/honest name and description, visible icon, at least one product scope but no more than necessary, redirect URIs entered (no more than necessary, https only), OAuth via App Login Flow credentials, working consent screen, API best practices (paging, rate-limit handling), no impact to user data on initial sign-up, branding compliance, user-permissions/privacy testing, and that the app enhances the Teamwork experience. You must provide a way for Teamwork to test the app. On approval the status flips to 'Published', 'available to everyone'.
approval.wait: 'Please allow up to 5 working days to get a response from our team' (stated for a response, not a guaranteed full approval time; no total duration stated)

blockers.detail: 'Your app will only have access to the data in the selected Teamwork.com account' until Teamwork verifies it. Nothing external works pre-verification.
blockers.howToClear: Build and test against your own account, then email integrations@teamwork.com with a testable app and the checklist items handled.
blockers.title: Single-account development cap

blockers.detail: On success 'the resulting payload will contain a permanent access token'. No refresh token, rotation, or access-token expiry is documented on the pages read. A leaked token is a long-lived credential.
blockers.howToClear: Vault tokens per installation and minimize exposure; there is no documented rotation to lean on.
blockers.title: Permanent token, no refresh flow documented

blockers.detail: The token response carries an apiEndPoint you must store and use per installation; Teamwork runs multiple data-center regions. Hardcoding one site's API base breaks other installs. Multi-account users are a real case; use userinfo.json.
blockers.howToClear: Persist apiEndPoint with each installation's token at exchange time.
blockers.title: Per-installation API endpoint

tested: Read-only verification: portal prerequisites, Publisher details, app creation, the App Login Flow, the verification process and checklist, and token behavior were checked against current apidocs.teamwork.com guides (no app created, nothing submitted)
unverified: Any verification fee; total approval duration beyond the 'up to 5 working days' first response; whether re-review is needed after post-publication scope/config changes.
Access-token expiry/revocation behavior (docs call it 'permanent'; no refresh token or revocation path documented).
Any numeric rate limit (only the 429 + ~60-second lockout behavior is described).
Whether unpublished apps can be installed by a limited set of external test accounts (docs say own account only).
The exact list of selectable Product Scopes in the portal (not enumerated in the docs read).

alternatives: Per-user API key / Basic (Bearer) auth (docs accept it for personal use and testing; the App Login Flow is the directed path for an app others use)
flavor.recommended: A single app in the Teamwork.com Developer Portal using the App Login Flow (Teamwork's OAuth 2.0), with only the Product Scopes it needs
flavor.why: Creating the app generates a client_id and client_secret (Credentials tab). There are no separate internal/public app types; the distinction is status: 'In development' vs 'Published'. Access is controlled by Product Scopes (per product: Teamwork/Projects, Desk, CRM, Spaces), not granular OAuth scopes: 'All APIs published on this portal allow you to access and update any data in your Teamwork.com account', so within a chosen product access is broad. Verification explicitly checks you requested 'no more than is necessary'.

humanMust: Be a user in the owner company of a Teamwork account (portal access requires it; users from other companies in the account cannot access the portal)
Set up Publisher Details (name, logo, website, privacy/terms URLs, VAT number, contact email, registered address)
Create the app and retrieve/vault the client_secret
Email integrations@teamwork.com to start verification and provide a way for Teamwork to test the app
name: Teamwork
nuances: The authorization code expires in 15 minutes; exchanging late returns 401. Sending the token-request body as URL params returns 400, and a non-POST request returns 405.

Redirect URIs 'must be secure URIs with https only unless they are using localhost' (the flow guide also mentions custom-protocol and Chrome-extension redirect URLs as passable). If your app has allowed origins, an additional origin header is required on the token request.
Scope changes re-trigger consent: 'adding new products will require you to re-authenticate to access APIs under the new scopes', and a consent screen appears again when scopes change.
Publisher details are a one-way-ish door: any user can set the publisher to start development, but 'once it's set, only a Teamwork.com Administrator can update these details'.

On HTTP 429, 'After 60 seconds, we'll let you back in!' (verification-page best-practices note). QA commonly rejects for mundane reasons: missing paging, ignoring 429s, data changes on sign-up, branding/privacy issues.
Portal roles: App Owners can update details/scopes/redirect URIs/origins, delete the app, update the secret, and manage app users; App Users can only edit name/description.
prerequisites: A user account in the owner company of a Teamwork account
Publisher Details (company/legal information used by Teamwork when validating the app)
At least one Product Scope and one redirect URL on the app

steps.detail: Portal access requires being a user in the OWNER company of a Teamwork account; users from other companies inside the account will not have access. On first portal login you are prompted for Publisher Details: name (shown on the consent screen), logo URL, website, privacy URL, terms URL, VAT number, contact email, registered address.
steps.title: Get portal access; set up Publisher Details

steps.detail: Name (shows on the consent screen), icon, description, Product(s) (at least one mandatory), Redirect URLs (at least one mandatory). Then open the app's Credentials tab for client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri; manage scopes and origins there.
steps.title: Create the app

steps.detail: Direct the user to teamwork.com/launchpad/login (generic) or {site}.teamwork.com/launchpad/login, with redirect_uri, client_id, and optional state. The user authenticates on Teamwork's side; Teamwork redirects to your redirect_uri with a code (valid 15 minutes) plus state if sent.
steps.title: Send the user to the launchpad login

steps.detail: POST JSON to teamwork.com/launchpad/v1/token.json with code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri (content-type application/json). The response contains the access_token (permanent, per the docs) plus installation info including the apiEndPoint to use for that installation. Call APIs with Authorization: Bearer; GET launchpad/v1/userinfo.json for user/installation info.
steps.title: Exchange the code; store token + apiEndPoint

steps.detail: While 'In development', the app works only on your own account. When ready, email integrations@teamwork.com to start verification and QA; allow up to 5 working days for a response. On approval the app is set to 'Published' and available to everyone.
steps.time: Email ~10 min; response up to 5 working days (stated)
steps.title: Request verification to go live

tagline: OAuth that works only on your own account until Teamwork's QA verifies you: an email-triggered review (response within up to 5 working days) stands between development and real users, and the token you get back is permanent, with no refresh flow documented.

time.active: ~30 min of portal setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
time.total: Days to weeks: verification response up to 5 working days (stated), total approval duration not stated
time.waiting: Up to 5 working days for the verification response (stated)
